items.title: Chapo reaffirms commitment to strengthening ties with international partners
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has reaffirmed his government’s commitment to strengthening diplomatic ties with international partners in order to foster the country’s development. The President was speaking on Thursday at a ceremony in which he received newly accredited diplomatic representatives, highlighting investment, business cooperation, technology transfer and skills development as priorities for promoting economic and social development. According to Maria Lucas, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Chapo welcomed the accreditation of the new representatives and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to strengthening relations of friendship and cooperation with the countries and institutions they represent. The diplomats are Martin Hackelberg from Germany, Brieu Pont from France, Lianne Houben from the Netherlands, Francisco Pardo from the European Union (EU), Ayça İnam from Türkiye, Dato Yusof from Malaysia, Roland Beridze from Georgia, Yury V. Nikalaichyk from Belarus, and Rod Rembendambya from Gabon.

items.title: Mozambique: Kenmare plans to extract strategic monazite ore in Nampula
items.summary: Mining company Kenmare Resources expects to produce and export at least 4,000 metric tons annually of Mozambique’s strategic monazite ore, according to company statements indicating plans to initiate licensing proceedings with the Mozambican Government The information was disclosed by Kenmare Resources Country Manager in Mozambique, Gareth Clifton, during the Conference on Value Addition Based on Available Minerals and Energy Resources held in Nacala, northern Mozambique. He noted that the miner is advancing plans to extract the mineral, which is recognized as a vital source of rare earth elements utilized in high-strength permanent magnets and advanced technologies According to the executive, a pre-feasibility study evaluating the extraction of monazite in Mozambique was completed two weeks ago “Initial results indicate that the project is viable, which is why we have initiated a definitive feasibility study.

items.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection The first confirmed Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe International Airport, according to African health officials, as new information from Switzerland contradicts Uganda's account of the Nigerian patient's travel history Uganda , a country reporting no active Ebola infections, has become a focus of investigations into cases thousands of kilometers apart Uganda insists it has no confirmed active cases of the deadly virus .

items.title: Muchanga expelled from Renamo for demanding Momade’s resignation
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – Renamo party, which used to be Mozambique’s main opposition movement, has decided to expel its best known former parliamentary deputies, António Muchanga, following his suspension last February. Muchanga was one of Renamo’s main speakers in the previous parliament (2019-2024). He continues to speak regularly in television talk shows. Together with demobilized guerrillas, Muchanga has been demanding the resignation of Ossufo Momade from his post as Renamo president. For many months Momade’s opponents have been occupying Renamo offices across the country, demanding his resignation, widely blamed for Renamo’s poor showing in the October 2024 general elections. The former guerrillas also claim that they are being persecuted and even murdered by the current Renamo leadership for demanding Momade’s resignation.

items.title: Japan-Russia ties erode as journalist sits in Moscow jail
items.summary: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. Moscow claims Tokyo is using journalists as spies Japanese Foreign Ministry officials were in Moscow this week in an attempt to contact a journalist arrested in Russia's far east on spying claims Journalist Yuki Imai was arrested on October 14 by Russia's FSB security service in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk on Sakhalin Island. Televised footage of the arrest showed FSB officers barging into his hotel room as he slept The correspondent for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper was accused of attempting to obtain information on soldiers in the region, which is near the Kiril islands, a geopolitical sore spot in Russia - Japan relations Russian authorities quickly transferred him to Lefortovo Prison in Moscow, where a court ordered him to be held in pre-trial detention until at least December 12.
